world.title: Montenegro expels Russian war blogger and four associates on security grounds
world.summary: Montenegro expelled Russian military blogger Mikhail Zvinchuk, founder of the pro-Kremlin Telegram channel Rybar, his wife and three associates on Oct. 9 after police and the National Security Agency detained them in Risan and revoked their right to stay on national and internal security grounds. Police said checks fou
world.content: Montenegro expelled Russian military blogger Mikhail Zvinchuk, founder of the pro-Kremlin Telegram channel Rybar, his wife and three associates on Oct. 9 after police and the National Security Agency detained them in Risan and revoked their right to stay on national and internal security grounds. Police said checks found their presence unacceptable and seized a drone, cameras and phones to determine how the equipment had been used. Prime Minister Milojko Spajić linked the operation to warnings of destabilization and hybrid warfare, while Rybar said the group was in Montenegro legally and planned to film a documentary, including at Cetinje Monastery. Zvinchuk said in a video that the group was being deported. Rybar has more than 1.5 million subscribers and has faced Western sanctions and U.S. allegations tied to election interference; Montenegrin authorities said they were examining the seized equipment.

world.title: Thieves steal 30,000 bottles in €5 million Tuscan wine heist
world.summary: Thieves stole about 30,000 bottles of prized wine worth an estimated €5 million from Marchesi Antinori’s Santa Cristina warehouse near Cortona, Tuscany, in Italy’s largest recorded wine theft, the producer said. The haul included Tignanello, Solaia and Guado al Tasso and was ready for export when thieves broke in on th
world.content: Thieves stole about 30,000 bottles of prized wine worth an estimated €5 million from Marchesi Antinori’s Santa Cristina warehouse near Cortona, Tuscany, in Italy’s largest recorded wine theft, the producer said. The haul included Tignanello, Solaia and Guado al Tasso and was ready for export when thieves broke in on the night of Oct. 3-4. The gang disabled alarms and surveillance cameras, then used the winery’s forklifts to load the wine into two trucks. Staff discovered the theft on Monday, Oct. 5, but Antinori announced it on Friday, Oct. 9, saying it had waited to avoid interfering with the investigation. Police and Carabinieri are reviewing surveillance footage and other evidence; no arrests had been reported. Antinori said it was warning customers worldwide to be wary of offers outside its official sales channels.
world.image_alt: Thieves steal 30,000 bottles in €5 million Tuscan wine heist

world.title: Saudi-led coalition says it destroyed 136 Houthi military targets
world.summary: The Saudi-led coalition said Saturday it had destroyed 136 Houthi military targets in a large-scale operation, while Houthi media reported Saudi strikes in Yemen’s Saada province. The campaign follows Thursday’s attacks on Riyadh’s King Khalid International Airport, which Saudi authorities said killed three people and
world.content: The Saudi-led coalition said Saturday it had destroyed 136 Houthi military targets in a large-scale operation, while Houthi media reported Saudi strikes in Yemen’s Saada province. The campaign follows Thursday’s attacks on Riyadh’s King Khalid International Airport, which Saudi authorities said killed three people and wounded others. The Houthis claimed responsibility. Houthi media also said Saudi strikes hit Sanaa airport and killed two people. The airport attacks damaged a Saudia aircraft and prompted airlines to cancel or suspend flights to Riyadh, though Saudi aviation officials said airport operations had returned to normal. The Houthis have renewed warnings against aircraft using Saudi airspace, and the European Union Aviation Safety Agency widened its flight-risk advisory. Riyadh is scheduled to host the WPC Energy Congress from Sunday, bringing together energy ministers, government officials and oil executives. Italy’s energy minister said he would participate remotely; organizers were still advertising the event on Friday.
world.image_alt: Saudi-led coalition says it destroyed 136 Houthi military targets

world.title: Gaza ceasefire reaches one year with withdrawal and disarmament stalled
world.summary: The U.S.-brokered Gaza ceasefire reached its first anniversary on Oct. 10 with key political and security provisions still blocked, Israeli strikes continuing and reconstruction barely begun. More than 1,400 Palestinians have been killed since the truce began, according to Gaza’s Health Ministry; almost all of the terr
world.content: The U.S.-brokered Gaza ceasefire reached its first anniversary on Oct. 10 with key political and security provisions still blocked, Israeli strikes continuing and reconstruction barely begun. More than 1,400 Palestinians have been killed since the truce began, according to Gaza’s Health Ministry; almost all of the territory’s roughly 2.1 million residents have been displaced during the war. Israel says Hamas must disarm before further troop withdrawals, while Hamas says disarmament must be linked to an Israeli withdrawal and an end to attacks. The agreement envisaged a Palestinian administration, an international stabilization force and reconstruction, but the administration has not entered Gaza and the force has not deployed. Israel has expanded the area it controls, and the ceasefire’s next phase remains stalled.
world.image_alt: Gaza ceasefire reaches one year with withdrawal and disarmament stalled

world.title: Mexican court convicts three men in 2024 surfers
world.summary: A judge in Ensenada, Mexico, found three men guilty on Friday, Oct. 9, of murdering Australian brothers Jake and Callum Robinson and their American friend Carter Rhoad during a surfing trip in Baja California in 2024. The judge found that the attack was premeditated and also convicted the defendants of armed robbery an
world.content: A judge in Ensenada, Mexico, found three men guilty on Friday, Oct. 9, of murdering Australian brothers Jake and Callum Robinson and their American friend Carter Rhoad during a surfing trip in Baja California in 2024. The judge found that the attack was premeditated and also convicted the defendants of armed robbery and armed carjacking. Prosecutors said the surfers were attacked during an attempted robbery. Baja California’s attorney general said the alleged ringleader tried to steal tires and other parts from the surfers’ pickup truck. The victims were shot, and their bodies were found in a well on May 3, 2024. The alleged ringleader’s former girlfriend testified that one victim pleaded for his life. The three men remain in custody and are due to be sentenced on Oct. 16. Prosecutors have requested a 210-year prison sentence for each defendant, although the maximum prison term in Baja California is 60 years.
world.image_alt: Mexican court convicts three men in 2024 surfers

world.title: Trump rebukes Norway after Nobel Peace Prize goes to Navi Pillay
world.summary: President Donald Trump criticized Norway after the Norwegian Nobel Committee awarded the 2026 Nobel Peace Prize to South African jurist Navi Pillay. Speaking at a rally in Syracuse, New York, on Friday, Trump called the decision “disgraceful and embarrassing,” described it as an “indelible stain” on Norway and said, “w
world.content: President Donald Trump criticized Norway after the Norwegian Nobel Committee awarded the 2026 Nobel Peace Prize to South African jurist Navi Pillay. Speaking at a rally in Syracuse, New York, on Friday, Trump called the decision “disgraceful and embarrassing,” described it as an “indelible stain” on Norway and said, “we will not forget, Norway.” He also dismissed Pillay as someone he had never heard of. Pillay, 85, a former International Criminal Court judge and U.N. human rights chief, was honored for her work promoting peace and international law. The Norwegian Nobel Committee said her work helped ensure the prosecution of war crimes, crimes against humanity and genocide. The State Department announced sanctions against the ICC on Friday, and a source familiar with the matter said the move had been brought forward after Pillay won the prize. The award ceremony is scheduled for Dec. 10 in Oslo.
world.image_alt: Trump rebukes Norway after Nobel Peace Prize goes to Navi Pillay

world.title: India detains youth leaders as Delhi restricts protest over voter-roll changes
world.summary: Indian police detained Cockroach Janta Party founder Abhijeet Dipke and two other movement leaders at Delhi airport on Oct. 10. Thousands of police and paramilitary personnel sealed parts of the capital ahead of a youth-led protest demanding the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar. Police detained
world.content: Indian police detained Cockroach Janta Party founder Abhijeet Dipke and two other movement leaders at Delhi airport on Oct. 10. Thousands of police and paramilitary personnel sealed parts of the capital ahead of a youth-led protest demanding the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar. Police detained hundreds of people in Delhi, while the party said at least 10,000 people had been detained nationwide. Police had not addressed the party’s claim. Authorities restricted transport, closed metro stations and suspended mobile internet near the protest area. The Supreme Court said some trains must run and metro stations should not face a blanket closure. The demonstrations target a nationwide voter-roll revision that has removed or flagged more than 130 million names in draft rolls. Critics say the changes risk excluding eligible voters, particularly from marginalised and minority communities, to benefit Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s Bharatiya Janata Party. The Election Commission says the exercise removes duplicate and ineligible entries and that wrongly excluded voters can re-enroll. A newspaper investigation said two election commissioners had repeatedly objected to aspects of the revision. Police said they denied permission because the application came late and cited public-order concerns. The movement insisted it would proceed. In a statement reported by DW, police said they detained about 500 people in Delhi. Protesters nevertheless attempted to reach the designated protest site at Jantar Mantar. State elections, including in BJP-governed Uttar Pradesh, are due to begin in early 2027.
world.image_alt: India detains youth leaders as Delhi restricts protest over voter-roll changes

world.title: Trump administration sanctions ICC, allowing 180 days to wind down dealings
world.summary: President Donald Trump’s administration imposed sanctions on the International Criminal Court as an institution on Friday, Oct. 9, blocking ICC assets under U.S. jurisdiction and requiring U.S. companies and individuals to wind down most dealings with the court within 180 days. Treasury licenses allow some operational,
world.content: President Donald Trump’s administration imposed sanctions on the International Criminal Court as an institution on Friday, Oct. 9, blocking ICC assets under U.S. jurisdiction and requiring U.S. companies and individuals to wind down most dealings with the court within 180 days. Treasury licenses allow some operational, technology, pension and detainee-related transactions to continue during the transition. Washington had previously sanctioned individual ICC judges and prosecutors. Secretary of State Marco Rubio said Washington was acting to prevent the court from prosecuting Americans. The United States has objected to ICC arrest warrants for Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and former defense minister Yoav Gallant, as well as its past investigation into U.S. personnel in Afghanistan. The court says it can prosecute crimes committed in territory within its jurisdiction, even when suspects come from non-member countries. The administration announced the sanctions hours after former ICC judge Navi Pillay received the 2026 Nobel Peace Prize, though it had made the decision before the award. The ICC condemned the sanctions and urged its 125 member states to help sustain its work. Eight countries, including Canada, France, Germany, Japan and the United Kingdom, said they strongly disagreed with the sanctions. EU officials said the six-month period left room for dialogue and that the bloc had options to protect the court’s operations.
world.image_alt: Trump administration sanctions ICC, allowing 180 days to wind down dealings

business.title: Anthropic bars repeated cruel treatment of Claude, updates AI rules
business.summary: Anthropic has added a ban on “sustained and needless abusive or cruel behavior” toward its Claude AI models, saying it applies only to extreme cases of repeated behavior with no discernible purpose. The ban excludes ordinary frustration, pushback, dark creative themes, model testing and research. The main enforcement m
business.content: Anthropic has added a ban on “sustained and needless abusive or cruel behavior” toward its Claude AI models, saying it applies only to extreme cases of repeated behavior with no discernible purpose. The ban excludes ordinary frustration, pushback, dark creative themes, model testing and research. The main enforcement mechanism remains Claude’s ability to end the interaction. Anthropic’s wider usage policy revision also clarifies rules on deceptive campaigns, election interference, weapons development, surveillance and law enforcement. The company said it had seen attempts to use its models to develop weapons guidance and control software. The revised policy is scheduled to take effect on November 12.
business.image_alt: Anthropic bars repeated cruel treatment of Claude, updates AI rules

business.title: OpenAI’s annualized revenue estimate near $50 billion rattles AI stocks
business.summary: OpenAI told investors its annualized revenue was approaching $50 billion at the end of September, about $20 billion below the roughly $70 billion figure that circulated the previous month. The gap does not represent lost sales or a missed company target: the higher figure was an investor estimate based on a different c
business.content: OpenAI told investors its annualized revenue was approaching $50 billion at the end of September, about $20 billion below the roughly $70 billion figure that circulated the previous month. The gap does not represent lost sales or a missed company target: the higher figure was an investor estimate based on a different calculation, not OpenAI’s own forecast. The discrepancy stems from how the companies count cloud-partner sales. Anthropic includes customer spending on its models through Amazon Web Services and Google Cloud, while OpenAI excludes those sales from its reported revenue. The different accounting methods complicate direct comparisons between the companies. Investors use their revenue figures to gauge AI demand and justify large infrastructure commitments. The news weighed on technology shares on Thursday, including chipmakers and companies with substantial AI investments or commercial ties to OpenAI. OpenAI is seeking at least $30 billion in new private funding at a reported $1.4 trillion valuation. Investors are also watching chip-sector earnings from ASML on October 14 and TSMC on October 15 for further evidence of hardware demand.
business.image_alt: OpenAI’s annualized revenue estimate near $50 billion rattles AI stocks

business.title: U.S. consumer sentiment falls to five-month low as prices rise
business.summary: U.S. consumer sentiment fell to 46.3 in early October from 48.1 in September, reaching its lowest level in five months, the University of Michigan’s preliminary survey showed. The reading was below the 47.8 economists had forecast in a Reuters poll. Reports on the survey attributed the decline to household frustration
business.content: U.S. consumer sentiment fell to 46.3 in early October from 48.1 in September, reaching its lowest level in five months, the University of Michigan’s preliminary survey showed. The reading was below the 47.8 economists had forecast in a Reuters poll. Reports on the survey attributed the decline to household frustration with higher prices, which the conflict in the Middle East has pushed up. Views of current economic conditions hit a record low, Bloomberg reported, while the survey’s director said consumers across political groups saw a weaker economic trajectory than at the start of the year. The October figure is a preliminary reading.
business.image_alt: U.S. consumer sentiment falls to five-month low as prices rise

business.content: OpenAI defended its dismissal of safety researchers Mikita Balesni, Tomek Korbak and Jasmine Wang, saying an internal investigation found they violated policies on handling sensitive information and uncovered a “significant breach of trust.” The company said it did not fire them for raising safety concerns or speaking out. The researchers dispute that account, saying they were fired for prioritizing safety. They warned that the handling of the firings could make colleagues afraid to raise concerns. The former employees urged OpenAI to maintain collaboration with independent safety groups and the ability to monitor advanced AI models. OpenAI said it is finalizing contracts with third-party assessors and plans to announce details in the coming weeks. It also agreed that monitoring requires an industry-wide commitment.

business.title: India objects to U.S. green-card freeze as Indian IT firms assess hiring
business.summary: India’s Ministry of External Affairs said the U.S. suspension of green-card processing for eight technology companies does not “advance the shared ambitions” of the two countries. It said the suspension could affect eligible workers’ residency applications but not existing H-1B visas. Indian firms and industry analysts
business.content: India’s Ministry of External Affairs said the U.S. suspension of green-card processing for eight technology companies does not “advance the shared ambitions” of the two countries. It said the suspension could affect eligible workers’ residency applications but not existing H-1B visas. Indian firms and industry analysts expect limited immediate business disruption but prolonged uncertainty for workers seeking permanent residency. Tata Consultancy Services said it filed fewer than 10 PERM applications in the past two years and does not expect the restriction to affect its workforce strategy or client work. The company reiterated its plan to hire 15,000 employees in the United States over five years. The suspension covers Microsoft, Adobe, Cognizant, Infosys, TCS, Wipro, HCL Technologies and Capgemini, and halts new and pending labor-certification applications involving them. Analysts said retaining experienced workers is the greater concern. They estimated that hiring locally in the United States costs 25% to 50% more than sending Indian employees, depending on the role. HFS Research expects companies to rely more on subcontractors, hire selectively in the United States and reassess offshore work over the next six to 12 months.
business.image_alt: India objects to U.S. green-card freeze as Indian IT firms assess hiring

business.title: EU and China agree to halve hybrid car exports over four years
business.summary: The European Union and China reached a preliminary understanding to reduce Chinese exports of hybrid and plug-in hybrid cars to the bloc by more than half over four years, EU trade chief Maroš Šefčovič said after two days of talks in Beijing on Oct. 9. The agreement is part of efforts to ease trade tensions and address
business.content: The European Union and China reached a preliminary understanding to reduce Chinese exports of hybrid and plug-in hybrid cars to the bloc by more than half over four years, EU trade chief Maroš Šefčovič said after two days of talks in Beijing on Oct. 9. The agreement is part of efforts to ease trade tensions and address the EU’s widening deficit with China, but how it will be implemented and how the reduction will be calculated remain unclear. FAZ cited EU sources estimating 600,000 to 800,000 vehicles, based on expected deliveries for the year. The understanding also covers improved access to the Chinese market for EU exports worth nearly €4 billion, including car parts, olive oil and footwear, and continued assistance with Chinese export licences for rare earths and permanent magnets. The European Commission said the market-access changes could save exporters at least €225 million in duties. EU leaders are due to assess the package at their Oct. 15-16 summit, after which officials expect to work out technical procedures. Šefčovič and China’s commerce minister, Wang Wentao, are scheduled to resume talks in January, with broader consultations in March 2027.
business.image_alt: EU and China agree to halve hybrid car exports over four years

business.title: Trump orders White House inquiry into Fed governor Lisa Cook
business.summary: President Donald Trump announced on Oct. 9 that he had established a White House committee to investigate mortgage-document allegations against Federal Reserve Governor Lisa Cook, renewing his effort to remove her. The panel plans a closed-door hearing on Nov. 5, at which Cook must answer questions. The White House say
business.content: President Donald Trump announced on Oct. 9 that he had established a White House committee to investigate mortgage-document allegations against Federal Reserve Governor Lisa Cook, renewing his effort to remove her. The panel plans a closed-door hearing on Nov. 5, at which Cook must answer questions. The White House says it will publish a transcript, and the committee will recommend whether there is legal “cause” to remove her. The allegations concern mortgage applications Cook submitted in 2021, before joining the Fed. Trump says she represented two properties as primary residences. Cook denies wrongdoing and has not been charged; her lawyers have described the matter as an inadvertent error. In June, the Supreme Court ruled 5-4 that she could remain in office while challenging Trump’s earlier removal attempt, finding that he had acted without giving her notice and an opportunity to respond. The inquiry follows the Fed’s unanimous Sept. 16 vote to raise its key interest rate, despite Trump’s calls for cuts. Cook is one of 12 voting members of the rate-setting committee, and the president’s renewed effort to remove her has prompted concerns about the central bank’s independence.
business.image_alt: Trump orders White House inquiry into Fed governor Lisa Cook

business.title: Hurricane Isaias cuts Gulf oil output as refineries face outage risks
business.summary: Hurricane Isaias made landfall near Destin, Florida, on Friday as a Category 2 storm with 105 mph winds, then weakened below hurricane strength by early Saturday. Offshore precautions cut Gulf of Mexico oil production by nearly 1.5 million barrels a day—about two-thirds of the region’s output and roughly 10% of U.S. pr
business.content: Hurricane Isaias made landfall near Destin, Florida, on Friday as a Category 2 storm with 105 mph winds, then weakened below hurricane strength by early Saturday. Offshore precautions cut Gulf of Mexico oil production by nearly 1.5 million barrels a day—about two-thirds of the region’s output and roughly 10% of U.S. production. The storm was expected to miss the Gulf Coast’s largest oil hubs, but outages could still affect refineries along its path. The two most exposed refineries, Chevron’s Pascagoula facility and Vertex’s Alabama refinery, together account for about 2.5% of U.S. refining capacity and 5% of Gulf Coast capacity. Pascagoula also supplies airports across the Southeast. Global gasoline and diesel supplies were constrained, and U.S. refineries were operating at 92.7% capacity. Companies evacuated offshore workers, shut safety valves below the ocean floor and moved mobile drilling facilities where possible. Without major power outages or damage, Gulf facilities typically take about a week to resume operations. Refinery restarts can be more complex because their processes depend on continuous power and heat.
business.image_alt: Hurricane Isaias cuts Gulf oil output as refineries face outage risks

science.title: IonQ reports quantum memory link with more than 1,000 entanglements per second
science.summary: IonQ said it demonstrated more than 1,000 entanglement events per second between a trapped-ion qubit and a silicon-vacancy quantum memory, describing the quantum interconnect as a record for ion-based systems. The company says the rate is more than four times its previous benchmark and could help link separate quantum
science.content: IonQ said it demonstrated more than 1,000 entanglement events per second between a trapped-ion qubit and a silicon-vacancy quantum memory, describing the quantum interconnect as a record for ion-based systems. The company says the rate is more than four times its previous benchmark and could help link separate quantum processors. A technical paper details the results of tests on working hardware, according to Quantum Zeitgeist. IonQ says the architecture could be adapted for neutral-atom and superconducting systems using signal transducers. The company is also pursuing broader compatibility through DARPA’s HARQ program.
science.image_alt: IonQ reports quantum memory link with more than 1,000 entanglements per second

science.title: Patients
science.summary: A study of 204 patients undergoing MRI found that listening to music they chose was associated with lower pain ratings 30 seconds and two minutes after insertion of an intravenous cannula. Mozart’s Sonata K448 was linked to reduced pain two minutes after insertion only among participants who already had pain; relaxatio
science.content: A study of 204 patients undergoing MRI found that listening to music they chose was associated with lower pain ratings 30 seconds and two minutes after insertion of an intravenous cannula. Mozart’s Sonata K448 was linked to reduced pain two minutes after insertion only among participants who already had pain; relaxation music and no music produced no significant reduction. Researchers assigned participants to groups by the order of their MRI appointments, not at random. The procedure caused brief, generally mild pain, limiting how widely the findings apply to other treatments. The researchers plan to test other classical music and examine whether music can help with more severe pain. The University Hospital Zürich team intends to use music more often during radiology-related vein punctures, particularly for anxious or claustrophobic patients.

science.title: NASA invites companies to propose commercial stations before ISS retirement
science.summary: NASA on Oct. 9 issued its final request for proposals from U.S. companies for commercial space stations in low Earth orbit, part of its plan to maintain a human presence there after the International Space Station retires. NASA says the stations should support research, technology development, crew training and prepara
science.content: NASA on Oct. 9 issued its final request for proposals from U.S. companies for commercial space stations in low Earth orbit, part of its plan to maintain a human presence there after the International Space Station retires. NASA says the stations should support research, technology development, crew training and preparation for missions to the Moon and Mars. Proposals are due Dec. 8, 2026, and NASA expects to award contracts in spring 2027. NASA says it wants credible plans and strong technical execution from companies prepared to invest in stations and develop their own customers and markets; the economics must work, it says. The agency plans to support multiple contractors initially before selecting providers for later design, certification and services.
science.image_alt: NASA invites companies to propose commercial stations before ISS retirement

science.title: Seychelles survey estimates 183,000 giant tortoises on Aldabra Atoll
science.summary: A new survey estimates that about 183,000 adult and sub-adult Aldabra giant tortoises live on Seychelles’ Aldabra Atoll, a record figure that exceeds the country’s human population of about 122,000. Led by the Seychelles Islands Foundation and the University of Exeter, the study analyzed counts collected from 2018 to 2
science.content: A new survey estimates that about 183,000 adult and sub-adult Aldabra giant tortoises live on Seychelles’ Aldabra Atoll, a record figure that exceeds the country’s human population of about 122,000. Led by the Seychelles Islands Foundation and the University of Exeter, the study analyzed counts collected from 2018 to 2022 and provides the first rigorous, atoll-wide estimate since the late 1990s. The population remained relatively stable during the survey period. Researchers say continued protection is needed: longer, more frequent droughts could reduce food and shade, rising seas threaten low-lying habitat, and feral cats and black rats prey on eggs and hatchlings. The estimate provides conservation managers with a baseline for tracking future population changes.
science.image_alt: Seychelles survey estimates 183,000 giant tortoises on Aldabra Atoll

science.title: Panama earthquakes damage buildings, trigger evacuations and tsunami alerts
science.summary: Two earthquakes, initially reported at magnitude 7.7 and 6.6, struck southern Panama on Friday, Oct. 9, damaging buildings and prompting evacuations; a tsunami warning was later lifted. The first quake was centered about 10 kilometers southwest of Pitaloza Arriba in Herrera province, at a depth of 10 kilometers, and wa
science.content: Two earthquakes, initially reported at magnitude 7.7 and 6.6, struck southern Panama on Friday, Oct. 9, damaging buildings and prompting evacuations; a tsunami warning was later lifted. The first quake was centered about 10 kilometers southwest of Pitaloza Arriba in Herrera province, at a depth of 10 kilometers, and was felt in neighboring Colombia. Authorities reported injuries but no deaths as of Friday evening, while aftershocks continued. Reports of damage across central provinces included collapsed or damaged buildings and fissures in roads. The airport briefly suspended operations, while Panama Canal traffic continued normally. Officials said structural checks would begin once tremors subsided, and the water and sewage authority reported interruptions at treatment plants following power outages.
science.image_alt: Panama earthquakes damage buildings, trigger evacuations and tsunami alerts

science.title: Researchers develop light-activated tattoos that can disappear without removal
science.summary: Researchers have developed PhotoTat, a tattoo ink system whose colors can appear, change or fade under particular wavelengths of light, allowing designs to become invisible without tattoo removal. The study was published Oct. 9 in Matter & Light; researchers say the pigments remain in the skin even when the design beco
science.content: Researchers have developed PhotoTat, a tattoo ink system whose colors can appear, change or fade under particular wavelengths of light, allowing designs to become invisible without tattoo removal. The study was published Oct. 9 in Matter & Light; researchers say the pigments remain in the skin even when the design becomes invisible. The inks could also be used for medical markings that need to be visible only during treatment, such as alignment marks for radiation therapy. Overall safety remains unproven. Only the purple ink has completed third-party medical tests and gone on sale; the researchers say more work is needed to bring other colors to market.
science.image_alt: Researchers develop light-activated tattoos that can disappear without removal

science.title: October skies bring Orionid meteors, Mars-Beehive pass and full moon
science.summary: October’s skywatching calendar includes the Draconid meteor shower, which peaked on the night of Oct. 8-9, and the Orionids, expected to peak around Oct. 21-22. The Orionids occur when Earth crosses dust left along the orbit of Halley’s Comet. Under dark skies, observers may see about 10 to 20 meteors an hour, though m
science.content: October’s skywatching calendar includes the Draconid meteor shower, which peaked on the night of Oct. 8-9, and the Orionids, expected to peak around Oct. 21-22. The Orionids occur when Earth crosses dust left along the orbit of Halley’s Comet. Under dark skies, observers may see about 10 to 20 meteors an hour, though moonlight could hide fainter ones. The best Orionid viewing is expected in the dark hours before dawn, after the moon sets. Other upcoming sights include Mars passing through the Beehive star cluster on Oct. 11 and October’s full Hunter’s Moon. EarthSky dates the full moon to the night of Oct. 25, while SciTechDaily lists Oct. 26.
science.image_alt: October skies bring Orionid meteors, Mars-Beehive pass and full moon

science.title: Curiosity captures six-image sunrise panorama of Mount Sharp on Mars
science.summary: NASA released a six-image panorama of rocky ridges on Mars that the Curiosity rover captured on Aug. 11, 2026, about an hour after sunrise. The ridges, called yardangs, lie on Mount Sharp in Gale Crater; the rover team aims to reach their foothills in 2027. Scientists say the ridges’ color and tilted rock layers differ
science.content: NASA released a six-image panorama of rocky ridges on Mars that the Curiosity rover captured on Aug. 11, 2026, about an hour after sunrise. The ridges, called yardangs, lie on Mount Sharp in Gale Crater; the rover team aims to reach their foothills in 2027. Scientists say the ridges’ color and tilted rock layers differ from the surrounding terrain. Volcanic ash is one possible origin, but the team says the formation’s composition remains unknown and will require close-up measurements with Curiosity’s instruments.
science.image_alt: Curiosity captures six-image sunrise panorama of Mount Sharp on Mars

sports.title: Mourinho backs Mbappe and confirms Real Madrid forward will start
sports.summary: Real Madrid coach Jose Mourinho defended Kylian Mbappe against criticism of his travel during injury recovery and recent photographs, calling the uproar “ridiculous” before Saturday’s La Liga match against Villarreal. Mourinho confirmed the France forward would start, saying he had met his club obligations. Mbappe inju
sports.content: Real Madrid coach Jose Mourinho defended Kylian Mbappe against criticism of his travel during injury recovery and recent photographs, calling the uproar “ridiculous” before Saturday’s La Liga match against Villarreal. Mourinho confirmed the France forward would start, saying he had met his club obligations. Mbappe injured his left knee while playing for France against Turkey on September 25. Mourinho said Mbappe returned to Madrid for scans, then consulted a specialist in France because of his history of knee problems. The club and the specialist agreed on the diagnosis, and Mbappe followed a recovery plan. Mourinho said the Paris venue was hosting a private Fashion Week event and the bicycles in Switzerland were used to get around a hotel complex. He also urged Bernabeu supporters to be fair as Madrid resumed its league campaign.
sports.image_alt: Mourinho backs Mbappe and confirms Real Madrid forward will start

sports.title: 49ers activate Mykel Williams for NFC West matchup
sports.summary: The San Francisco 49ers activated defensive end Mykel Williams from the physically unable to perform list, clearing the 2025 first-round pick to make his season debut Sunday against the Seattle Seahawks. sports.content: The San Francisco 49ers activated defensive end Mykel Williams from the physically unable to perform list, clearing the 2025 first-round pick to make his season debut Sunday against the Seattle Seahawks. Williams tore his ACL in Week 9 last season and returned to practice last week. He joins a defensive line missing Nick Bosa, who is out with a calf injury. Seattle defensive tackle Leonard Williams was cleared to play after missing Thursday’s practice with an ankle injury. Safety Ty Okada is also available. The 49ers are 4-0 and the Seahawks are 3-1 entering the NFC West matchup in Seattle, their first meeting since Seattle eliminated San Francisco from last season’s playoffs.

sports.content: Golden State and Atlanta swept their WNBA semifinal series Friday, setting up a Finals matchup that opens Oct. 17 at Chase Center. The second-year Valkyries beat the defending champion Las Vegas Aces 87-77 in overtime, while the Dream edged the New York Liberty 85-83. Golden State will have home-court advantage; both franchises are seeking their first WNBA championship. The Valkyries erased a nine-point halftime deficit against Las Vegas and outscored the Aces 16-6 in overtime. Kayla Thornton led Golden State with 18 points, and Gabby Williams added 16, including eight in the extra period. In New York, Angel Reese scored 22 points for Atlanta, while Jordin Canada had 19 points and 11 assists. The Dream won without leading scorer Allisha Gray, who was sidelined by a hand injury. Golden State’s defense ranked among the best in league history, while Atlanta created extra possessions by forcing turnovers and collecting offensive rebounds. The Dream are 5-0 in the playoffs, and the Valkyries needed three games to get past Dallas in the first round before sweeping the Aces.

sports.content: Australia reached 196-6 early on day two of the first Test against South Africa in Durban, with Matt Renshaw unbeaten on 51 and captain Pat Cummins on 37 after their partnership lifted the tourists from 124-6. Bad light had ended the opening day after 65.2 overs. Nic Maddinson returned to Test cricket nearly a decade after his previous appearance, having undergone treatment for testicular cancer diagnosed in April 2025 that had spread to his lung and lymph nodes. He was bowled for zero after facing 33 balls, the longest scoreless innings by an Australian Test opener and the third-longest by any opener. Steve Smith made 25 and passed Steve Waugh to become Australia’s third-highest Test run-scorer, with 10,945 runs. South Africa’s pace bowlers took all six wickets despite the absence of injured Kagiso Rabada and Lungi Ngidi, with Marco Jansen, Wiaan Mulder and Anrich Nortje sharing the wickets. The match is the first of a three-Test World Test Championship series. Former Australia opener Matthew Hayden criticised Maddinson’s selection, saying selectors were “disrespecting first-class cricket”.

sports.content: Manchester United could give £70m summer signing Carlos Baleba his debut against Tottenham at Old Trafford on Saturday, October 10, after both sides made poor starts to the season. United sit 12th with five points from five league games, while Tottenham are bottom with two points; managers Michael Carrick and Roberto De Zerbi face pressure over their teams’ results. Baleba, a 22-year-old Cameroon midfielder, joined from Brighton while recovering from an ankle injury and has not yet played for United. He brings pace, defensive ability and the ability to retain possession under pressure. Opponents have found space through the middle of United’s midfield. His debut is possible, but his fitness and match sharpness leave his role uncertain. United are also without Benjamin Sesko and Patrick Dorgu, while Noussair Mazraoui is a doubt; Spurs can call on centre-backs Micky van de Ven and Jan Paul van Hecke, but Pedro Porro and Mykhailo Mudryk are unavailable. United face away games against Leeds, Atlético Madrid, Como and Chelsea later in October.

sports.content: Leicester Tigers recovered from a 14-0 deficit to beat Gloucester 38-31 at home on Friday, earning their first home win of the season. Aaron Wainwright scored his first try for Leicester as the hosts built a 21-14 halftime lead and held on for victory. Gloucester opened the scoring while Leicester fly-half Billy Searle was in the sin-bin but suffered their first league defeat of the season. Late tries and a penalty earned Gloucester two bonus points, keeping them top of the Prem. Prince Harry attended the match at Mattioli Woods Welford Road and received a mixed reception from spectators.

sports.content: West Indies beat India by six wickets in Ranchi on Friday, chasing 250 with nine balls remaining to level the five-match T20 series at 1-1. Their total of 252-4 was the highest successful chase in West Indies T20 international history and the second-highest in men’s T20Is, behind South Africa’s 259 in 2023. Captain Shai Hope finished unbeaten on 102 from 45 balls, while Sherfane Rutherford struck 84 from 37. Their 120-run fourth-wicket stand revived the chase after India’s Mayank Yadav took two wickets in the opening over. Hope and Romario Shepherd then completed the chase, with Shepherd making 34 not out from 13 balls. India posted 249-5, built around Sanju Samson’s 82 from 41 balls and a late burst from Shreyas Iyer and Tilak Varma. The teams meet in the third match in Indore on Sunday, October 11, with the series level.

sports.content: Arsenal manager Mikel Arteta said his conscience was clear about his three years as Manchester City’s assistant manager, answering “Yes” when asked directly at his first news conference since an independent commission announced its findings. He urged respect for the unresolved process and declined to say whether he had spoken to Pep Guardiola. Manchester United manager Michael Carrick said the case had affected him personally and that receiving a winners’ medal later could not change how it felt to lose a title race at the time. He called for a swift resolution. Liverpool manager Andoni Iraola said uncertainty was bad for everyone involved and acknowledged Liverpool supporters’ anger. City manager Enzo Maresca rejected the idea that the club’s titles were tainted and said he trusted its leadership. Arsenal host Leeds on Saturday after the international break, and Liverpool are due to play City at Anfield on Sunday.
